newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise, but heavies fall - Feb 13.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise, but heavies fall - Feb 13.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices advance Thursday in line with WTI/Cushing markets, while California heavy grades added to yesterday's declines after another regional oil company lowered their postings.
Heavy crude buyers found it difficult to locate sellers who would do deals at a $3.00 discount to postings, yesterday's confirmed deal.
"We were interested in buying at prices like that, but they didn't return our phonecalls," one trader said, referring to Tosco, which sold to Celeron Wednesday at $3.00 off.
Outright prices for heavies fell with lower postings, ranging $12.75/14.75 a barrel after Unocal lowered their Kern River buying price by around 50 cents a barrel.
BP America, the dominant seller of Alaska North Slope crude, declined to give an offer price Thursday, as they assessed the market.

Traders said they heard Chevron's crude processor at the El Segundo plant remained shut longer than expected for planned maintenance , forcing the company to sell a cargo of ANS to Shell at $1.10 two day ago. The sale came a day after the refinery bought from a cargo from BP at $1.15 under WTI.
"Their problems at El Segundo are a little more serious than people thought. They sold because they're long crude," one trader said.
